items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And then I joined Wings... We did — one song we did, “Baby’s Request” was a demo for the Mills Brothers.

ctx.x: Yeah, and then after you’re done it feels weird because a person comes out —

Yeah. It’s a kind of reality check. But I mean this really goes along with the ambition to be a studio musician was just it doesn’t matter who you’re playing with it’s making music. I mean it looks good on the resume to have — that record with Rosemary Clooney was really cool. And I was 24, 25 at the time. It was mid-70s in London and she was making a comeback and she was on tour with Bing Crosby. It was not long before he died. And it was just a very cool experience, you know, playing with somebody of that kind…
And they called you at Apple.

items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: as were Lennon McCartney and Ringo and Harrison, as far as they were listening to that stuff and then creating a British version of it.

ctx.x: Do you listen, do you recall listening for the bass notes?

Oh totally. I listened to all the parts. We had Radio Luxembourg, was, you know, broadcast from the continent, so it wasn’t restricted to the same playlists that the BBC had, which was, at that time, we didn’t have Radio One, Radio Two until somewhat later. 1963, ’64 it was The Light Program or The Home Service or whatever. So you got a very eclectic mix there anyway. But Radio Luxembourg was all-American top 40. So that’s where I heard all those records. I heard Motown Records for the first time. And I’d be ©…

listening to what the rhythm section was doing, and how the bass and the kick drum work together, as were Lennon McCartney and Ringo and Harrison, as far as they were listening to that stuff and then creating a British version of it. In fact the first time a Motown song was ever played on British radio was by The Beatles in 1962. I forget which song it was. But it was a live broadcast and they played a Motown song. Because you didn’t hear that, and then you did. Then all of a sudden you started to hear that…

items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was in Wings from ’78 to ’81.

ctx.x: I was in Wings from ’78 to ’81. And the picture next to that is Paul McCartney with a concertina sitting on the balcony of a castle, a twelfth century castle on the south coast of England when we were recording. The one above that is Linda McCartney at a Hammond B3 organ, and you can’t really see clearly but on top of the organ there is a pack of Senior Service, Players Senior Service cigarettes, no filtertips, which is what Paul smoked at the time. There’s a cup of tea, a scotch and Coke, a bunch of boxes of…
Well I have a burning question here, do your grandchildren get to play with your guitars?
